headline: In 1962, divinity students were given magic mushrooms in church to see if they would meet God.
slides: Good Friday at Boston University's Marsh Chapel. A service was about to start.
Twenty divinity student volunteers were split into two groups. Nobody knew which group they were in.
Ten were given psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms. Ten got niacin, which only makes you tingle.
It was designed by Walter Pahnke, a Harvard graduate student, to test whether the drug could trigger a mystical experience.
His supervisors were Timothy Leary and Richard Alpert. Leary was dismissed from Harvard the following year.
Researcher Rick Doblin tracked down most of the students more than two decades later to ask what it had meant to them.
sources: Sources: Walter Pahnke, Drugs and Mysticism (Harvard, 1963); Rick Doblin, Journal of Transpersonal Psychology (1991)
